facts.text: A false alarm is a warning when nothing dangerous is present; a nuisance alarm concerns something real that is not dangerous in the situation; alarm accuracy is the share of all alarms that deserved a response.
facts.quote: A false alarm is a warning given when nothing dangerous is there, a nuisance alarm is a warning about something real that is not dangerous in the situation, and alarm accuracy is the share of all alarms that deserved a response.

facts.text: The best off-road alarm-performance numbers remain those from a 2004 field test, published in 2006, of a radar warning system on a Caterpillar 793B haul truck over seven days at a US copper mine.
facts.quote: The best off-road numbers are still from a 2004 field test, published in 2006, of a radar warning system on a Caterpillar 793B haul truck over seven days at a US copper mine

facts.text: In the Caterpillar 793B radar warning system field test, 102 of 580 alarms (18%) were false alarms.
In the Caterpillar 793B radar warning system field test, 243 of 580 alarms (42%) were nuisance alarms.
facts.quote: Of 580 alarms, 102 (18%) were false, 243 (42%) were nuisance

facts.text: In the Caterpillar 793B radar warning system field test, 235 of 580 alarms (40%) warranted action.
facts.quote: Of 580 alarms, 102 (18%) were false, 243 (42%) were nuisance, and 235 (40%) warranted action.

facts.text: The Caterpillar 793B radar warning system field test recorded no missed detections.
False alarms in the Caterpillar 793B radar warning system field test came from ruts, rocks, foliage and the truck's own rear tires.
facts.quote: False alarms came from ruts, rocks, foliage and the truck's own rear tires

facts.text: The audible alarm of the Caterpillar 793B radar warning system was found switched off after shifts during the field test.
facts.quote: the audible alarm was found switched off after shifts

facts.text: No study defines a false alarm rate that off-road operators will accept.
facts.quote: No study defines a false alarm rate that off-road operators will accept

facts.text: An 18% false alarm rate caused problems in the off-road field test, but that does not establish that a 17% or 5% false alarm rate would be acceptable.
facts.quote: an 18% rate caused problems, but it does not follow that 17% is acceptable or that 5% would be

facts.text: The old system's false and nuisance alarm rates are the baseline that the new system must beat.
facts.quote: The old system's false and nuisance rates are the baseline the new system must beat

facts.text: A fair measurement of the old and new systems' false and nuisance alarm rates requires an independent record of what was really present.
facts.quote: they can only be measured fairly against an independent record of what was really there

facts.text: The continued status of the figure published in 2006 as the best hard off-road alarm-performance number demonstrates how thin the independent off-road data are.
facts.quote: That the 2006 figure is still the best hard number shows how thin the independent off-road data are
